pairedExternal.interpretation: Candidate minus incumbent on the exact same deal-seed and partnership-seat clusters. Positive means improvement.

cardPlayExperiment.status: promoted to Standard after independent internal and matched external gains

training.conditioning: Soft Gaussian likelihood of observed normal bids under frozen learned bidder, sigma0.85; approximate model, not calibrated human posterior. No rejection sampler; finite proposals always weighted. Candidate disables nil when any prior nil was observed, an unsupported training context.
training.target: Actual nil-minus-normal hand score differential with accumulated bags

evaluation.baseline: Frozen non-nil learned bidder, identical nil-aware heuristic card play

pairedExternal.interpretation: Candidate minus incumbent on the exact same deal-seed and partnership-seat clusters. Positive means improvement.

nilUtilityExperiment.status: rejected for Standard: internal improvement failed to transfer; external score deficit worsened

evaluation.baseline: Frozen learned bidder; identical heuristic card play
evaluation.releaseDecision: rejected: no independently confirmed incumbent improvement

research.recommendation: Warm-start card play from strong public-information teachers, then train score-aware action values against a frozen league of strong and varied opponents, with budgeted information-set search. Weak-only self-play produced a nil bidder that failed the external test. This is a project-specific direction, not a universal best-method claim.

sources.title: Learning hidden-card distributions for trick-taking search

research.unbenchmarked: AI Factory and NeuralPlay expose no public batch-evaluation interface found. Loddyluo Spades-AI uses materially different scoring. Released TricksterBots is a credible external baseline; no world-champion ranking is established.

limitations: No calibrated Elo rating, human-strength estimate, or verified world-champion claim.
The baseline is a modest documented heuristic; bidding and search tests answer separate questions.
Nil utility is learned against a frozen play policy; its success predictions are not calibrated for human opponents.
Determinization assumes heuristic rollout opponents and can suffer strategy fusion.
Node measurements are not phone latency guarantees.
